Pursuant to Section 3-05 of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules, the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) intends to enter into negotiations for a five-year agreement with Fund for Public Health in New York, Inc. (FPHNY) for the purchase of grant acquisition, fundraising, grant management and project management needs.

FPHNY was created in 2002 as an independent nonprofit organization to partner closely with NYC DOHMH to further its mission of improving the health of all New Yorkers. FPHNY contributes to the advancement of public health in NYC by: a) soliciting funds for both project and general support from public and private funding sources and donors who would or could not ordinarily support government initiatives, and; b) by providing a vehicle for effective administration of grant funds for pilot projects or time-sensitive grant programs. FPHNY is the only non-profit organization that is solely dedicated to soliciting funding, facilitating partnerships, and providing administrative support to advance DOHMH's public health priorities. As such, it plays a unique role and does not duplicate the efforts of other agencies or organizations.

notices.short_title: DOP FY27-28 AIM Program Contract with USA
notices.description:
In accordance with Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Probation (DOP) is requesting approval to extend the existing contract with Union Settlement Association, Inc., (USA) through a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) to support the continuation of services under the Advocate, Intervene, Mentor (AIM) Program. The contract term is from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028 for an amount of $1,083,500.26 for this period. 

The AIM Program is an Alternative to Placement (ATP) intervention designed for high-risk, justice-involved youth on probation. The program provides intensive, community-based mentoring through a one-on-one model that pairs participants with paid advocate-mentors who are available around the clock and serve as consistent, trusted supports. Advocate-mentors are credible messengers with strong ties to the communities served and lived experience that enables effective engagement with participants. Over an approximately six- to nine-month, court-mandated period, youth receive individualized support focused on improving decision-making, strengthening family and community connections, and reducing further justice sys…
notices.plain: The Department of Probation awarded Union Settlement Association Inc. a $1,083,500 contract extension through June 30, 2028, to continue its Advocate, Intervene, Mentor (AIM) program, which provides community-based mentoring for high-risk, justice-involved youth on probation.

This NA is needed for DHS to have more time to determine options for a new  mens city owned assessment site by 7/1/27. Agency needs about 6 months for an appropriate assessment site creation as this process includes the extensive adjustments to the building layout, security assessments and other staffing needs. Hence DHS needs to keep 357 Marcus Garvey as a provider operated site until the assessment of this and other DHS sites are completed.
notable.plain: The Department of Homeless Services awarded United Cerebral Palsy Associations of New York State a $9.3 million negotiated extension to operate the 200-bed Marcus Garvey emergency shelter in Brooklyn through June 30, 2027.

notable.short_title: DOP FY27-28 AIM Program Contract with USA
notable.description:
In accordance with Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Probation (DOP) is requesting approval to extend the existing contract with Union Settlement Association, Inc., (USA) through a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) to support the continuation of services under the Advocate, Intervene, Mentor (AIM) Program. The contract term is from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028 for an amount of $1,083,500.26 for this period. 

The AIM Program is an Alternative to Placement (ATP) intervention designed for high-risk, justice-involved youth on probation. The program provides intensive, community-based mentoring through a one-on-one model that pairs participants with paid advocate-mentors who are available around the clock and serve as consistent, trusted supports. Advocate-mentors are credible messengers with strong ties to the communities served and lived experience that enables effective engagement with participants. Over an approximately six- to nine-month, court-mandated period, youth receive individualized support focused on improving decision-making, strengthening family and community connections, and reducing further justice sys…
notable.plain: The Department of Probation awarded Union Settlement Association Inc. a $1,083,500 contract extension through June 30, 2028, to continue its Advocate, Intervene, Mentor (AIM) program, which provides community-based mentoring for high-risk, justice-involved youth on probation.
